title: RE:cover - Internet-based therapy for survivors of intimate partner violence
summary:
Experiences of intimate partner violence are a widespread phenomenon that poses a significant health risk to those affected. A number of studies have shown an increased prevalence of various mental disorders among those affected. The ICD-11 distinguishes between post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and complex post-traumatic stress disorder (C-PTSD) in this area. Symptoms of C-PTSD appear to be associated with prolonged or repeated relationship trauma, including experiences of domestic or intimate partner violence, which are also named as possible events in the diagnostic criteria. Initial study results are already available for the treatment of these specific symptoms, but these focus primarily on victims of child abuse. Specific therapy programs for the alleviation of cPTSD in victims of intimate partner violence are not yet available in German-speaking countries. 
The aim of the study is to develop and evaluate the first German-language, therapist-supported, and internet-based intervention for reducing symptoms of complex post-traumatic stress in survivors of intimate partner violence. A therapeutic manual has been developed for this purpose, tailored to the specific needs of the target group and its efficacy will be investigated.

interventions.name:
intervention group
The intervention group receives password-protected access to a designated study website. There, they work through specially developed modules that are organized according to different topics (e.g., strengthening emotion regulation). The modules contain psychoeducational content a

wait-list control group
The waiting group also receives the intervention after the waiting period (8 weeks) has expired.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Symptoms of complex posttraumatic stress disorder
- Sufficient German language skills, reading and writing ability
- Access to the internet and an internet-enabled device
- Informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Ongoing threat or danger posed by perpetrator(s)
- Acute suicidality
- Current substance dependence or (severe) substance abuse
- severe dissociative symptoms
- other current psychotherapeutic treatment
- Changes in the dosage of psychotropic drugs within the last 6 weeks
- Cognitive or physical impairments that would limit participation in therapy on a written basis
